title: 'PFI UiTM turut perlu disiasat – KMUiTM
body: 'Kolektif Mahasiswa UiTM (KMUiTM) menggesa Suruhanjaya Pencegahan Rasuah Malaysia (SPRM), Jawatankuasa Kira-Kira Wang Negara (PAC) dan Jabatan Audit Negara menyiasat keseluruhan projek Inisiatif Pembiayaan Swasta (PFI) UiTM, susulan perkembangan terbaharu mengenai tatakelola dan pengurusan kewangan UiTM Holdings. Menurut KMUiTM, perhatian terhadap UiTM Holdings tidak sepatutnya menyebabkan persoalan PFI UiTM yang melibatkan komitmen konsesi jangka panjang dan nilai kewangan yang dianggarkan berbilion ringgit kembali dilupakan, khususnya apabila persoalan mengenai kaedah perolehan dan kos konsesi projek itu telah dibangkitkan sejak 2014. Pada 2014 Rafizi Ramli mempersoalkan enam projek kampus UiTM di Pasir Gudang, Jasin, Seremban 3, Puncak Alam, Tapah dan Kota Samarahan yang menurutnya diberikan melalui rundingan terus, termasuk kepada syarikat-syarikat yang dikaitkan dengan ahli sebuah parti politik. Beliau menganggarkan kos pembinaan enam kampus tersebut sekitar RM1.8bn, berbanding kira-kira RM8.6bn jumlah bayaran konsesi yang didakwanya sepanjang tempoh 23 tahun. Rafizi turut mencabar kerajaan mendedahkan perjanjian konsesi supaya kos, keuntungan pemegang konsesi dan struktur perjanjian dapat diperiksa umum. Pada masa sama, PAC pada ketika itu turut mempersoalkan ketelusan enam projek tersebut dan menggesa maklumat mengenai projek konsesi didedahkan kepada umum, termasuk persoalan penggunaan rundingan terus serta sama ada kerajaan memperoleh value for money. Rekod rasmi Parlimen menunjukkan UiTM menerima RM881j peruntukan pembangunan pada 2022, tetapi RM858j atau 97.3% peratus daripadanya diperuntukkan untuk caj tetap PFI yang merangkumi ‘availability charges, maintenance charges dan maintenance reserve fund’. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member Pada 2023 pula, RM865j atau 95.0% daripada RM911j peruntukan pembangunan diperuntukkan bagi caj tetap PFI. KMUiTM berkata angka tersebut menimbulkan persoalan mengenai kos lepas (opportunity cost) PFI kepada universiti. Setiap ringgit yang diperuntukkan untuk memenuhi komitmen konsesi jangka panjang tidak boleh digunakan pada masa yang sama untuk keperluan pembangunan lain seperti penyelenggaraan kampus, naik taraf fasiliti, pelaksanaan program pembangunan mahasiswa, pengambilan tenaga akademik tetap, pembinaan kolej kediaman serta kebajikan mahasiswa. “Persoalannya bukan sekadar berapa kos sebuah kampus dibina. Persoalannya ialah berapa jumlah yang dibayar sepanjang hayat konsesi dan apa yang UiTM terpaksa korbankan kerana sebahagian besar peruntukan pembangunannya terikat kepada komitmen tersebut,” menurut KMUiTM. Bagi KMUiTM, hakikat bahawa PFI masih mempunyai komitmen kewangan yang aktif menjadikan persoalan lama itu relevan untuk diperiksa semula, bukannya sekadar diarkibkan sebagai kontroversi 2014. Tuntutan itu turut mengambil kira perkembangan terhadap UiTM Holdings. PAC pada 2024 mengenal pasti kelemahan dalam tadbir urus kewangan serta kelemahan maklumat dan kawal selia pengurusan pelaburan UiTM Holdings – manakala SPRM kini menjalankan siasatan terhadap kerugian syarikat berkenaan dan beberapa isu berkaitan, termasuk isu pembayaran RM42j berkaitan projek solar Gambang yang menurut SPRM dibuat bagi tujuan yang tidak berkaitan dengan projek tersebut dan tanpa kelulusan lembaga pengarah. Perbandingan itu, kata KMUiTM, bukan bermaksud mendakwa PFI dan UiTM Holdings melibatkan kesalahan yang sama. Sebaliknya, ia menimbulkan persoalan mengenai standard akauntabiliti terhadap wang awam UiTM. Pada Januari 2026, persoalan tersebut telah pun diketengahkan oleh wakil KMUiTM dalam sidang media mahasiswa mengenai sistem perolehan universiti awam. Mereka ketika itu turut mengangkat semula konsesi kampus UiTM yang dibangkitkan Rafizi pada 2014 dan mengaitkan isu perolehan universiti dengan amanah kewangan awam, selain menggesa audit forensik terhadap projek dan tender universiti. KMUiTM kini menggesa supaya keseluruhan portfolio PFI UiTM dibuka kepada siasatan dan audit, termasuk proses penganugerahan kontrak asal, penggunaan rundingan terus, struktur pemilikan syarikat konsesi, jumlah bayaran yang telah dibuat, baki komitmen, kos penyelenggaraan dan penilaian value for moneyberdasarkan prestasi sebenar projek. Kumpulan itu turut menggesa kerajaan mendedahkan jumlah keseluruhan komitmen PFI yang masih berbaki dan menilai kos lepas kepada fungsi pendidikan UiTM akibat peruntukan pembangunan yang terikat kepada caj PFI. Menurut KMUiTM, penelitian tersebut juga penting kerana PFI bukan semata-mata model pembiayaan yang sudah ditinggalkan. UiTM masih mengurus portfolio PFI, dan sebarang cadangan untuk memperluas penggunaan model tersebut, termasuk bagi projek infrastruktur atau tenaga, perlu dibuat hanya selepas prestasi dan kos kontrak sedia ada dinilai secara bebas. Kewujudan kampus PFI juga didakwa menyebabkan pembinaan kolej kediaman baharu dan penambahan kemudahan kampus lebih rumit, memandangkan kampus-kampus berkenaan secara teknikalnya ibarat bangunan yang disewa oleh UiTM. KMUiTM berkata penyiasatan semula tidak bertujuan menghukum sesuatu model pembiayaan secara automatik, tetapi memastikan keputusan yang mengikat wang awam untuk puluhan tahun dapat dipertanggungjawabkan berdasarkan kos sebenar, prestasi sebenar dan manfaat kepada universiti. “Kalau benar PFI memberikan value for money, maka kerajaan perlu membuktikannya berdasarkan lebih sedekad data sebenar, bukan sekadar hujah ketika kontrak mula diberikan,” menurut kumpulan itu. – KMUiTM The views expressed in Aliran's media statements and the NGO statements we have endorsed reflect Aliran's official stand. Views and opinions expressed in other pieces published here do not necessarily reflect Aliran's official position.

title: 'CIMB IB Says Malaysia Could Widen Corporate Tax Base for Budget 2027, Cut Old Deductions
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 5): Malaysia could widen its corporate tax base by reviewing special and double deductions that have been in place for two to three decades, and remove deductions that no longer serve their original purpose, said CIMB Investment Bank. CIMB IB said, citing KPMG senior adviser on tax policy Dr Verrinderjeet Singh during a discussion, that the removal of selected deductions could lead to the government collecting more revenue while creating room for a lower headline corporate tax rate. “His [Verrinderjeet] proposal is selective: investment incentives remain important for attracting businesses, but their benefits need closer scrutiny. He links Malaysia’s shift towards outcome-based incentives to its response to Global Minimum Tax,” said CIMB IB. It added, “Their effectiveness will depend on monitoring whether investors deliver the intended economic benefits”. Malaysia’s headline corporate income tax rate is currently 24%, but the amount of tax companies ultimately pay is also affected by deductions, exemptions and investment incentives. On major tax changes, CIMB IB said Malaysia is unlikely to introduce new tax changes in Budget 2027, with stronger collection from existing taxes and a wider tax base offering the main scope for raising government revenue. The government is expected to focus on improving tax collection, particularly by bringing more businesses into the tax net and identifying income that is not fully reported. Smaller businesses are likely to offer more room for additional collections, as larger companies are already more visible to the tax authorities, said CIMB IB. “His central message was that stronger collection and targeted refinements to existing taxes offer the main near-term revenue opportunities. Against a continued focus on cost-of-living support and the social agenda, he expects few substantial tax changes in the coming budget,” said CIMB IB. E-invoicing could help identify unreported taxable activity, although smaller businesses face additional compliance and technology costs. CIMB IB said Veerinderjeet expects participation to broaden as economic conditions improve. CIMB IB also sees scope for greater use of data analytics by the Inland Revenue Board (IRB) and Customs to identify businesses and income outside the existing tax net. On indirect taxes, CIMB IB said Veerinderjeet does not expect the goods and services tax (GST) to return in Budget 2027. Instead, the focus is likely to remain on improving the existing sales and service tax (SST). SST is estimated to cover about 78% to 80% of goods and services, approaching the breadth of the former GST regime. CIMB said broader exemptions for business inputs could reduce the cascading of tax costs through supply chains, although this would come at the cost of lower tax receipts. Veerinderjeet also does not expect an increase in the 2% dividend tax on annual dividend income above RM100,000, an extension of capital gains tax to listed shares or a further increase in the 30% top personal income tax rate in Budget 2027, according to the note. “Dr Veerinderjeet argues that the government should ‘sweat our assets’ through better collection, supported by greater investment in tax agency analytics. These efforts can deliver incremental gains, while broader personal, corporate and indirect tax bases offer scope to lift tax-to-GDP towards 15% over time,” said CIMB IB economists. Veerinderjeet estimates only 15% to 16% of the workforce currently pays personal income tax, with low wages limiting the number of taxpayers. Higher wages would therefore be important in expanding the personal income tax base. Budget 2027 is expected to be tabled in Parliament on Oct 9. title: 'IOI Properties Gets Bursa Securities Approval for RM7.58b REIT Listing
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): IOI Properties Group Bhd (KL:IOIPG) said Bursa Malaysia Securities has approved the listing of its proposed RM7.58 billion IOIPG Malaysia Real Estate Investment Trust (IOIPG REIT) on the Main Market. In a filing on Thursday, the property developer said Bursa Malaysia Securities had, via a letter dated Sept 30, approved the admission of IOIPG REIT to the Official List of Bursa Securities, and the listing and quotation of its 5.5 billion units under the REITs sector. Bursa Malaysia Securities also approved the listing and quotation of up to 300 million new units to be issued as payment of management fees to IOI REIT Management Sdn Bhd — the REIT’s manager. The approval marks another step forward for the listing of IOIPG REIT. IOI Properties received approval from the Securities Commission Malaysia (SC) last month for listing of the trust that will house RM7.58 billion worth of retail, office and hotel assets. The target was to complete the listing before the year ends. Other assets include the IOI City Towers and PFCC Towers, as well as six hotels — Putrajaya Marriott Hotel, Le’ Meridien Putrajaya, Moxy Putrajaya, Four Points by Sheraton Puchong, W Kuala Lumpur and Courtyard by Marriott Penang. It also plans to pay out at least 90% of its distributable income on a quarterly basis. The RM7.58 billion acquisition will be satisfied through the issuance of 5.5 billion units at 90 sen each, alongside RM2.65 billion in cash to be funded through sukuk issuance. As part of the proposed offering, 715.61 million units will be offered under the retail portion, including 550.61 million units through a restricted offer for sale to existing IOI Properties shareholders. Eligible shareholders will be entitled to one REIT unit for every ten IOI Properties shares held on an entitlement date to be announced later. Another 55 million units will be allocated to eligible persons, while 110 million units will be made available to the Malaysian public. The institutional offering, meanwhile, will comprise up to 1.48 billion units, including 687.5 million units for Bumiputera investors approved by the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (Miti), with up to 796.89 million units allocated to other Malaysian and foreign institutional and selected investors. On Sept 14, the company revised the planned use of proceeds. It cut the allocation for debt repayment to RM1.53 billion, or 32.9%, from RM3.04 billion, or 65.6%. It raised the allocation for project development, property investment and related activities to RM3.07 billion, or 66%, from RM1.55 billion, or 33.6%. Total proceeds were put at RM4.66 billion, assuming the over-allotment option is not exercised, compared with RM4.62 billion previously. Shares of IOI Properties were down by five sen or 1.5% to RM3.41 at Thursday’s trading day break, giving it a market value of RM18.8 billion. Year to date, its shares have increased by 28.68%. title: 'IOIPG Malaysia REIT to Pay Out Quarterly Dividends, List With Assets Worth RM7.66b
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 24): IOIPG Malaysia REIT is planning to pay out at least 90% of its distributable income on a quarterly basis, as the real estate investment trust seeks listing on the Main Market. The trust is listing with properties in Klang Valley and Penang worth RM7.66 billion combined, according to its draft prospectus. The trust also has the right-of-first-refusal to acquire local assets owned by its sponsor IOI Properties Group Bhd (KL:IOIPG). IOIPG Malaysia REIT will also consider assets of other owners though the priority will be retail, office, industrial and hospitality properties in urban and suburban areas in Malaysia. The proposed initial public offering (IPO) will allow IOI Properties Group to trim its debt from an acquisition spree involving over RM1 billion in 2024. The developer is also considering spinning off its Singapore properties worth RM26 billion into another real estate investment trust. The listing of IOIPG Malaysia REIT was approved by the Securities Commission last month and the target was to complete the listing before the year ends. The IPO will be split into retail and institutional tranches, offering up to 40% of the total issued fund size upon listing. Institutional investors, including cornerstone investors, will be allocated 27% of the total units. Cornerstone investors — typically large institutional investors such as pension funds and insurers — commit to taking up a portion of the IPO shares before they are marketed to other retail and institutional investors. Their presence helps to build up other investors’ confidence to invest in the IPO. Under the retail tranche, shareholders of IOI Properties Group are entitled to 10% of the units on offer on the basis of one unit for every 10 existing shares of the developer held on a date to be determined later. The Malaysian public will only be allocated 2%, while eligible persons under pink form allocation get up to 1% of total units. Net proceeds from the listing will accrue entirely to IOI Properties Group after covering estimated listing expenses totalling about RM4 million. Maybank Investment Bank and AmInvestment Bank are the joint principal advisers, global coordinators, bookrunners, managing underwriters and underwriters. DBS Bank is the joint global coordinator and joint bookrunner. CIMB Investment Bank, Hong Leong Investment Bank, RHB Investment Bank and UOB Kay Hian are the joint bookrunners and underwriters. Oversea-Chinese Banking Corp is also one of the bookrunners. title: 'Daily Newswatch - 30 Sep 2026
body: 'The FBM KLCI ended 1.6% lower at 1,644 points on Tuesday, hitting a ninemonth low as broad-based selling pressure weighed on the market. Sentiment was dampened by rising oil prices and bond yields hovering near multi-year highs, as investors braced for interest rates to remain elevated for longer. Financial Services (-1.7%), Transportation & Logistics (-1.5%) and Property (-1.4%) led sectoral declines, dragged by RHB Bank (-3.8%), Tenaga Nasional (-1.5%) and Nestle Malaysia (-1.2%). Market breadth remained weak, with 684 losers against 412 gainers, while 556 counters were unchanged. Asian markets closed mostly lower on Tuesday as elevated oil prices and US Treasury yields weighed on risk appetite. South Korea’s KOSPI fell 0.3% to 6,870.8, Taiwan’s TAIEX declined 0.8% to 47,632, Japan’s Nikkei 225 slipped 0.6% to 65,481.3, and Hong Kong’s Hang Seng eased 0.5% to 24,523.6. In contrast, the Shanghai Composite gained 0.2% to 3,830.5. In South Korea, losses were recorded in LG Energy Solution (-3.30%), Hyundai Motor (-1.55%), Hanwha Aerospace (-2.22%), and Doosan Enerbility (-2.93%), while weaker domestic business sentiment added to the cautious tone as the BOK’s business sentiment index fell for the first time in three months in September. In China, gains were led by Guangzhou Automobile (+10.0%), Greenland Holdings (+6.4%) and China Fortune (+6.2%), supported by expectations of increased government bond issuance in 4Q26 as Beijing steps up fiscal support to shore up slowing economic growth and weak domestic demand. European equities edged higher on Tuesday as easing oil prices reduced inflation concerns and lowered expectations of an imminent ECB rate hike. The STOXX 50 gained 0.3%, while the STOXX 600 was little changed, with technology stocks leading gains. ASML jumped 4%, while energy stocks weakened as Brent crude eased toward USD104/barrel. Julius Baer surged 7%, while Lindt & Sprüngli fell 8.4% after cutting its sales-growth outlook. US stock indices closed mostly lower on Tuesday as rising Treasury yields and elevated oil prices weighed on sentiment. The S&P 500 fell 0.2% and the Dow shed 130 points, while the Nasdaq gained 0.2%. The 10-year yield climbed to levels last seen in 2007, while the 30-year yield hovered near 2004 highs. Tech stocks were mixed, with Alphabet and Nvidia down 0.5% and 0.7%, respectively, while Meta, Oracle, Broadcom and Micron gained 3.2%, 4.0%, 1.6% and 1.0%, respectively, amid optimism following plans for an Anthropic IPO. US: 10 Year Treasury Note Yield to 5.28% on Tuesday The yield on the US 10-year Treasury note resumed its climb to 5.28% on Tuesday, holding at 2007 highs, while the 30-year rate surpassed 5.6% to touch a 2002 dot-com bust level. Global government bonds have come under pressure as Middle East-driven oil price gains fuel expectations that central banks, including the Federal Reserve, will raise interest rates further. Swaps traders are pricing in nearly a full percentage point of Fed rate hikes over the coming year. In the US, strong economic activity, along with concerns over large fiscal deficits and rising government debt, is also weighing on the bond market. (Trading Economics) US: Job openings fall in August; layoffs remain low US consumer confidence fell in September to the lowest level since 2014 as pessimism grew about the economy and the labour market. The Conference Board’s gauge of confidence decreased 6.7 points to 81.9 after a downward revision to the prior month, data released Tuesday showed. The median estimate in a Bloomberg survey of economists was 89. (Bloomberg) US: Consumer confidence plunges to lowest level since 2014 Job openings, a measure of labour demand, had dropped by 256,000 to 7.079 million by the last day of August, the Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics said in its Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey, or Jolts report, on Tuesday. Data for July was revised higher to show 7.335 million vacancies instead of the previously reported 7.271 million. (Reuters) US: Gold ticks up after hitting over seven-week low; US data in focus Gold prices edged higher on Tuesday after hitting a more-than-seven-week low in the previous session, as investors watch for US economic data that could offer clues on the US Federal Reserve's (Fed) interest rate outlook. Spot gold rose 0.6% to US$4,140.10 (RM16,899.89) per ounce, as of 0856 GMT, after hitting its lowest level since Aug 5 on Monday. US gold futures gained 0.1% to US$4,171.60. (Reuters) US: Bond market is getting closer to sounding alarm on US economy The Eurozone Economic Sentiment Indicator fell to 97.9 in September 2026 from 98.4 in August, below market expectations of 99.0. It marked the first decline in sentiment since April, as consumers became more concerned about rising oil prices and stalled negotiations to end the sixmonth US-Iran war. Consumer confidence deteriorated to -16.5 from -15.5, while inflation expectations rose to 35.2 from 33.0. (Bloomberg) EU: Area Economic Sentiment Indicator The Eurozone Economic Sentiment Indicator fell to 97.9 in September 2026 from 98.4 in August, below market expectations of 99.0. It marked the first decline in sentiment since April, as consumers became more concerned about rising oil prices and stalled negotiations to end the six-month US-Iran war. Consumer confidence deteriorated to -16.5 from -15.5, while inflation expectations rose to 35.2 from 33.0. (European Commission) UK: Set to pay highest yield since 1999 at 10-year bond auction The UK government is set to pay the highest yield since 1999 at an upcoming auction of 10-year debt, as investors demand additional premiums to compensate for persistent inflation and the prospect of spending increases in next month’s budget. Britain’s Debt Management Office is scheduled to sell up to £4.25 billion (US$5.6 billion or RM22.95 billion) of 4.875% coupon bonds maturing in July 2036 on Tuesday. (Bloomberg) UK: Mortgage approvals fall to 32-month low as loan costs bite Demand for home loans unexpectedly fell in August as higher borrowing costs triggered by the Iran war put off prospective homebuyers. The number of mortgage approvals fell for a second consecutive month to 54,918 from a downwardly revised 55,928 in July, the Bank of England said Tuesday. It was the lowest figure since December 2023. Economists expected no change. (Reuters) CN: Said to offer cheap loans to help state firms pay overdue bills China has started offering low-cost funding to help local government-affiliated firms settle unpaid bills, according to people familiar with the matter, expanding efforts to mend corporate balance sheets and remove one of the biggest bottlenecks for investment. The People’s Bank of China (PBOC) set up a new relending facility to provide cheap capital to commercial and policy banks, they said, asking not to be identified discussing a decision that hasn’t been made public. (Reuters) CN: Expands targeted lending to bolster economy, cuts PSL rate China announced several steps to encourage banks to lend to targeted sectors including infrastructure and technology, in an attempt to juice growth after a months-long slowdown in the economy. The People’s Bank of China increased the quota for a relending programme supporting technological innovation and equipment upgrades by 200 billion yuan (US$28 billion or RM114 billion), bringing the total to 1.4 trillion yuan, according to a statement Tuesday. (Bloomberg) CN: Offers mortgage subsidies to boost ailing property sector China will subsidise mortgage interest payments for first-time homebuyers nationwide, as policymakers step up efforts to revive the housing market amid a prolonged property downturn and slowing economic growth. First-home buyers will get subsidies worth an annualised rate of one percentage point of the mortgage principal, according to a Ministry of Finance statement late Tuesday. To qualify, homes must be 120 square meters or smaller and priced at 1.5 million yuan (US$224,000 or RM913,337) or less. (Bloomberg) CN: Signals economic stimulus to counter worsening slowdown China has given its strongest signal yet that it will move with greater urgency to counter a deepening slowdown, as the government promised to introduce new measures to support the economy and study policies to stabilise the reeling property market. The authorities will “put in place a package of practical and effective additional policies” as they seek to “strengthen counter-cyclical adjustments” to achieve this year’s economic and social development goals, according to a statement issued after a Monday meeting of the State Council, China’s cabinet chaired by Premier Li Qiang. (Bloomberg) SK: Monthly Industrial Statistics, August 2026 South Korea’s industrial production unexpectedly dropped 4.8% month-on-month in August 2026, falling well short of market expectations for a 0.5% increase and reversing an upwardly revised 0.5% rise in July. It was the first decline in industrial production in three months and the steepest decline since May 2020, with manufacturing contracting 5.1% (vs 0.4% in July), weighed down by the automobile industry. Manufacturing production contracted for both domestic (-5.5% vs 1.2%) and overseas (-0.2% vs 4.1%) demand. (Statistics Korea) JP: August factory output falls 1.7% month-on-month Japan's factory output fell 1.7% in August from the previous month, versus the median market forecast for a 1.7% rise, government dat showed on Wednesday. Manufacturers surveyed by the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry expect seasonally adjusted output to increase 3.2% in September and grow 3.1% in October.(Reuters) JP: Retail Sales Growth Below Forecasts Retail sales in Japan increased 2.7% year-on-year in August 2026, below market expectations for a 3.3% rise and slowing from a downwardly revised 3.7% growth in the previous month. It was the sixth consecutive month of growth in retail activity, mainly boosted by a 17.7% surge in motor vehicle sales. title: 'Penang’s draft plan could open more of its hills to building
body: 'Kam Suan Pheng and Evelyn Teh “Rising from the sea in that first light of dawn that touches reality with a gentle charm, the Penang hills provide an unforgettable landmark for the visitor sailing in by sea. From the palm-fringed bays as yet a black indistinguishable smudge, the eye follows the flowing silhouette of the hills.” – Margaret Khor, The Straits Times Annual, 1960. Ask anyone who has crossed on the ferry, or driven over the bridge at dusk, and they will say the same: that green line of hills is how you know you are home. That silhouette is part of what makes Penang, Penang. Beyond the scenery, the hills are part of the island’s natural public infrastructure – one that is rarely counted. They hold soil, absorb and direct water, support forests and wildlife, and shape the landscape where we and our ancestors have lived. That landscape could change significantly if the draft State Structure Plan 2040 is adopted without stronger safeguards for hill and slope development. First, some background. The current Penang State Structure Plan 2030 does not allow development on land 76 metres (250 feet) or more above sea level, or on slopes of 25 degrees or steeper. There are limited exceptions for infrastructure and utilities. The limit is stricter than the national guideline. The state set it because it recognised how fragile, and how important, the island’s hills are. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member The 2030 plan reads: Sebarang Pembangunan Perbandaran Yang Meliputi Pembangunan Skim Perumahan Perhotelan Resort Perdagangan Perindustrian Dan Sebarang Struktur Bangunan Footprint Tidak Dibenarkan Di Kawasan:- - Kawasan Tanah Tinggi Yang Diwartakan Di Bawah Akta Pemeliharaan Tanah 1960 Akta 385 Atau - Sebarang Tanah Yang Berada Pada Aras 76 meter 250 kaki) Ke Atas Atau - Kawasan Berkecerunan 25 Darjah Ke Atas KECUALI Bagi Pemajuan Infrastruktur Dan Utiliti Dibenarkan Dengan Syarat Syarat Dari Jabatan Teknikal Yang Berkaitan Dan Mendapat Kelulusan Dari Pihak Berkuasa Negeri. In English: Any urban development, including housing schemes, hotels, resorts, commercial or industrial developments, and any building structures, is prohibited in the following areas: - Highland areas gazetted under the Land Conservation Act 1960 (Act 385); or - Any land situated at an elevation of 76 metres (250 feet) or higher; or - Areas with a slope gradient of 25 degrees or steeper; EXCEPT for infrastructure and utility developments, which are permitted subject to conditions imposed by relevant technical departments and approval from the State Authority. The key concern The state government rolled out a new draft 2040 plan in August – years before 2030 arrives. It will overwrite the previous version. The draft 2040 plan says: Strategi Perancangan PS3-1: Pembangunan di Kawasan Khusus yang Melebihi Ketinggian 76 meter. Strategi ini merupakan pendekatan perancangan yang memberi kelonggaran kawalan ketinggian bangunan secara terpilih di kawasan khas yang telah dikenal pasti sebagai kawasan tumpuan pembangunan strategik. Pelaksanaan strategi ini bertujuan mengoptimumkan penggunaan tanah yang terhad melalui pembangunan berintensiti tinggi dan berorientasikan transit, khususnya di pusat bandar, koridor ekonomi dan kawasan pesisir yang mempunyai kapasiti infrastruktur mencukupi. Walau bagaimanapun, kebenaran ini tertakluk kepada penilaian teknikal terperinci seperti kesesuaian guna tanah, nisbah plot, kawalan kepadatan, impak trafik, keselamatan, impak visual serta pematuhan kepada garis panduan reka bentuk bandar dan kajian impak alam sekitar. In English: Planning Strategy PS3-1: Development in Special Areas Exceeding a Height of 76 Metres. This strategy is a planning approach that allows for selective flexibility regarding building height controls in specific areas identified as strategic development hubs. Its implementation aims to optimize limited land use through high-intensity, transit-oriented development, particularly in city centres, economic corridors and coastal areas with adequate infrastructure capacity. However, such approval is subject to detailed technical assessments covering aspects such as land-use suitability, plot ratio, density controls, traffic impact, safety, visual impact, and compliance with urban design guidelines and environmental impact studies. In plain terms, the 2040 draft swaps ‘don’t build there’ (in the 2030 plan) for ‘build there if the paperwork says it’s safe’. The 2030 plan took a precautionary approach: keep away from the risk altogether. The 2040 draft replaces it with case-by-case approval, where each project’s own technical studies decide whether a hill can take it. Are these adequate safeguards, or is this a problem waiting to happen? Why change the limit? The threshold of 76m above sea level was not arbitrary. It was a deliberate safeguard that Penang chose to keep. Penang had adopted stricter controls than the national KSAS (environmentally sensitive areas) elevation framework, which it is now reverting to. The Safety Guideline for Hillsite Development (second edition, 2020) says Penang Island covers roughly 285 sq km. About 40% of it is Class 3 and Class 4 land, with slopes steeper than 25 degrees. The first version of the guideline went further. It reduced the footprint of buildings on hill land to make slopes safer and keep more green areas. Now these precautions are set aside. The 2040 draft presents this as a development strategy, not as a finding that the 76m limit is irrelevant. Outside the draft, no new evidence, assessment or policy review shows that the precautionary approach is no longer needed. What evidence, then, supports such a significant change in risk management? Look closely at the numbers. The highest point in Penang is 833m above sea level, but the horizontal area of the hills is small. The slopes are therefore compressed into a limited range of height and width. Add the complex pattern of hills and ridges, and very few pockets of land are flat enough to build on without cutting into the surrounding slopes. Even if building is allowed on isolated pockets, the roads needed to reach them must cross steeper terrain. Their environmental impact will reach far beyond the site. We do not have to imagine what that looks like. In October 2017, a landslide at a construction site in Tanjung Bungah killed 11 workers. A year later, part of a ‘paired road’ at Bukit Kukus collapsed during construction, killing nine. Bukit Kukus was a road, exactly the kind of infrastructure the 2030 plan already allowed as an exception. If the exception alone could cost so many lives, what happens when the rule itself is lifted? This is probably why past planners chose the 76m (250ft) limit. That wisdom applies even more today, as climate change brings heavier and more frequent rain to fragile hills. And what happens on the hill does not stay on the hill. These slopes feed the Air Itam and Teluk Bahang dams that fill our taps. When forests can no longer hold the rain, it runs down into lowland streets as flash floods. One does not need to live on a hill to pay for what happens on one. Paperwork is not landscape planning Some may argue that a technical assessment before approval is a reasonable safeguard. It can tell us whether a project meets existing standards. These include the Penang Safety Guideline for Hill Site Development 2020, the EIA Guidelines for Development in Slope and Hill Areas issued by the Department of Environment, and the planning and management guide for environmentally sensitive areas by PLANMalaysia. But none of these answers the bigger question: how many projects can these hills absorb before the whole system gives way? The 2040 draft says hill development control is strengthened through risk assessment, including the environment’s carrying capacity and climate resilience. Any development on hill land between 300 and 1,200 metres, or between 150 and 300 metres, and on slopes above 25 degrees, must submit a geotechnical risk assessment and a climate risk assessment. However, we know of no publicly accessible study or official database that gathers the information needed as a baseline. This should be established before the first hill or slope proposal is submitted. It seems the draft simply adopted a guideline written for the highlands of the peninsula – not one drawn up for Penang island. Could we, or should we? With today’s engineering, there are many ways to stabilise a slope: retaining walls, modern drainage, soil nails, piles and engineered slopes. A project may well be shown to be safe on paper. But the natural slope will have been substantially altered. Its long-term safety then rests on things no approval can guarantee. These include construction quality, drainage maintenance, inspection, the capacity and funding of the agencies responsible, extreme weather and future changes in land use. The irony is that a retaining wall is only as safe as the last time someone cleared its drains. There is also no baseline of existing conditions or of the role the hills play. That role covers the watershed, ecological corridors, natural drainage and geological formations. Penang lacks a hill and slope master plan that understands how sensitive and connected the hills are. Only such a plan can properly define, map and measure the hills’ carrying capacity, including projected climate scenarios. So the question shifts. We could make hill and slope development safe. But should we, and at what cost, when we have no baseline data and no guarantee these projects will stay safe in the long term? A project being technically safe is not the same as the landscape being safe. Gazette first, assess later When a gazetted state structure plan marks an area as potentially developable, the effects ripple out quickly. Land values rise, investors form expectations, land changes hands, proposals are drawn up and contracts are signed. All of this happens long before any environmental impact or technical assessment is complete. That order of events tilts the outcome. Once money and contracts are committed, rejecting a project on environmental grounds carries legal and financial consequences. The seemingly rational way out is to reduce every risk to an ‘acceptable’ level and hope nothing goes wrong later. The assessment no longer decides whether to build, only how. Show us the evidence The 2040 draft marks a significant shift from precautionary restriction towards risk-based conditional development. That may be reasonable in some circumstances. But the draft must show why the previous limits are no longer needed. It must also explain how project-by-project checks will deal with risks that build up across the landscape, worsen with climate change and cannot be undone once a hill is cut. If Penang is deliberately moving beyond the precautionary framework to create more development opportunities, it should show us the evidence. That means the thresholds and landscape-level safeguards that justify the change, in the form of a hill and slope development master plan, published before the 2040 plan is gazetted, not after. In the end, for most of us, this is not really a debate about slope angles, geotechnical reports or even the state structure plan. It is about the hills we know, some of us since childhood. These are the hills we see from our windows, or on the drive home after a long day at work. On them lie the green trails we climb at weekends to take in the view of our beloved Penang from above. It is also about feeling safe when the torrential rain comes. Can we sleep soundly knowing the hills near us will keep doing what they have always done: holding the soil, soaking up the water and slowing the runoff before it reaches our neighbourhoods? Or will we rely more and more on concrete walls and drains to protect us from hills we ourselves have altered? Dr Kam Suan Pheng is a soil scientist and co-founder of Penang Hills Watch, with a doctorate in agronomy-soil from Cornell University. Evelyn Teh is a Penang-based public policy researcher and environmental scientist specialising in ecological management, climate change and urban studies. The views expressed in Aliran's media statements and the NGO statements we have endorsed reflect Aliran's official stand. Views and opinions expressed in other pieces published here do not necessarily reflect Aliran's official position.

title: 'Mahkamah Tinggi kekalkan anugerah RM77 juta kepada kontraktor utama Menara Merdeka
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Mahkamah Tinggi mengekalkan keputusan Tribunal Timbang Tara menganugerahkan RM77 juta kepada kontraktor utama Menara Merdeka Maybank (sebelum ini dikenali Menara Merdeka 118) .   Keputusan tribunal menghendaki Global Wall (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd (GWM) membayar RM77,022,327.67 kepada Samsung C&T Corporation UEM Construction JV Sdn Bhd (SUJV) membabitkan pertikaian kerja fasad bagi projek mercu tanda berkenaan.   Pesuruhjaya Kehakiman, Rajes Raghavuji menolak permohonan GWM mencabar keputusan itu, dengan memutuskan isu dibangkitkan sama ada secara individu atau kumulatif, gagal melepasi syarat bagi membolehkan keputusan tribunal diketepikan mengikut Akta Timbang Tara.

title: 'Maybank, UPSI santuni komuniti menerusi pendidikan dan kreativiti
body: 'TANJONG MALIM – Hampir 200 warga Maybank dari seluruh Perak berganding bahu dengan Universiti Pendidikan Sultan Idris (UPSI) menjayakan program kesukarelawanan berteraskan pendidikan, kreativiti dan pemerkasaan komuniti menerusi Maybank Group Global Corporate Responsibility (CR) Day 2026.  Program yang berlangsung di Kampus Sultan Azlan Shah itu merupakan kerjasama pertama Maybank Group Global CR Day dengan UPSI menerusi Pusat Pembangunan Akademik dan SULAM@UPSI.  Timbalan Naib Canselor (Akademik dan Antarabangsa) UPSI, Prof Dr Raja Nor Safinaz Raja Harun berkata, program bertemakan “Impacting Society Positively, Enabling Well-Being for All” itu mencerminkan komitmen bersama sektor industri dan institusi pendidikan tinggi dalam menghasilkan impak positif kepada masyarakat.  “Pendekatan ini selari dengan aspirasi UPSI untuk menghubungkan ilmu, pendidikan dan kepakaran universiti dengan keperluan sebenar komuniti,” katanya.  Menurut beliau, dua modul SULAM@UPSI yang mempunyai elemen keusahawanan dan kelestarian serta menyasarkan golongan berkeperluan khas dipilih bagi program berkenaan.  Ia membabitkan SULAM Sen-Care daripada Fakulti Pembangunan Manusia (FPM) dan Creative Heritage For Good daripada Fakulti Seni, Kelestarian dan Industri Kreatif (FSKIK).  Raja Nor Safinaz berkata, UPSI berharap program itu menjadi pemangkin kepada kerjasama strategik lebih luas bersama Maybank, khususnya dalam pembangunan bakat, pendidikan, keusahawanan, inovasi, kesukarelawanan dan pemerkasaan komuniti.  “UPSI berharap penganjuran ini bukan sekadar program sehari, sebaliknya menjadi titik permulaan kepada lebih banyak kerjasama strategik pada masa hadapan,” katanya.  Sementara itu, Timbalan Pengarah Pusat Pembangunan Akademik UPSI, ChM Dr Yuhanis Mhd Bakri berkata, hampir 200 warga Maybank dari cawangan di Perak menyertai program berkenaan.  Menurutnya, Maybank Group Global CR Day merupakan inisiatif kesukarelawanan yang menghimpunkan warga institusi perbankan itu di pelbagai negara untuk melaksanakan aktiviti memberi manfaat kepada masyarakat dan alam sekitar.  Pengarah Wilayah Maybank Perak, Suresh Ramasamy pula berkata, kerjasama dengan UPSI membuka ruang kepada warga Maybank mendekati masyarakat melalui aktiviti kesukarelawanan yang lebih bermakna.  “Maybank Group Global CR Day bukan sekadar aktiviti kesukarelawanan, tetapi platform untuk warga Maybank menyumbangkan kemahiran, masa dan tenaga kepada masyarakat.  “Kerjasama dengan UPSI memberi nilai tambah apabila warga Maybank dapat berganding dengan mahasiswa dan warga universiti melaksanakan aktiviti kreatif, inklusif serta memberi manfaat kepada komuniti,” katanya.  Beliau berkata, program itu turut membolehkan warga Maybank, mahasiswa UPSI dan komuniti berkongsi pengalaman, kemahiran serta kepakaran menerusi aktiviti yang dirangka untuk menghasilkan manfaat secara langsung.  Katanya, kolaborasi tersebut memperlihatkan kekuatan hubungan universiti, industri dan komuniti apabila UPSI menyumbangkan ilmu serta bakat, industri membawa pengalaman dan sumber, manakala masyarakat mendapat manfaat daripada kerjasama berkenaan.  Keterangan gambar: Warga UPSI bersama kira-kira 180 kakitangan Maybank dari Perak menjayakan Maybank Group Global Corporate Responsibility (CR) Day 2026 di Kampus Sultan Azlan Shah, UPSI.
